rationale: The from_pov and _reorient code is the same in both solutions, so the difference is only in path_to. A uses the textbook backtracking pattern: push the current node, check whether it is the target, recurse into the children, and pop on failure. Because of that, the case where the start node is also the target needs no special handling. B starts the path with the root, has the helper push children rather than the current node, and needs an extra guard (tree.label != to_node) to cover the root being the target. That spreads the logic over two places and is harder to follow. Both have the same side effect of mutating the original tree, so A's simpler, more uniform recursion is slightly better.
